  - region "Simple English explanation of Polynomial Inequalities":
    - paragraph: In simple English
    - heading "Understand Polynomial Inequalities" [level=2]
    - paragraph: A polynomial inequality uses a sign chart at the roots. (x−1)(x−2)(x−3) is negative on (2,3), zero at 1,2,3, and positive at x=4. You can learn Polynomial Inequalities by trying one small example instead of long theory.
    - paragraph: "Mark every root, test a point in each open interval, and include roots when equality is allowed. Example: Solve (x - 1)(x - 3)(x + 2) >= 0. Mark roots -2, 1, and 3. Test signs on each interval. So the answer is [-2,1] and [3,infinity)."
    - paragraph: "In real life, curve design: Keep a curve above an axis. Watch out: Forgetting a root where sign does not cross. Mark every root and test intervals."
    - complementary:
      - generic: Try this example
      - paragraph: Solve (x - 1)(x - 3)(x + 2) >= 0.
      - generic "Compare your answer"
